Next year.

the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

He drives fast.

examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?

Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Polite (вы) or plural. Core Russian det meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Who are your rivals?
Is this your programme?
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come back, to return', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.trans: I'll be back soon.
He came back home.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening
E.g. a school evening. Common masculine noun meaning 'evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Good evening!
I'll call in the evening.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: instrumental of вечер used as an adverb

examples.trans: Come in the evening.
I'm at home in the evening.
Well, come in the evening.

meanings.en: to turn off, switch off, shut down
meanings.note: + acc. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ключить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn off, switch off', paired with 'выключать'.

examples.trans: Slavik, turn off the television, please!
I turned off the light in the room.
Yes, Mama. I turned it off.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('sad, gloomy').

examples.trans: Why are you so sad?
It's a sad story.
So why so gloomy?

meanings.note: Also 'girlfriend' (моя девушка). Common feminine noun meaning 'young woman; girlfriend' in everyday Russian.
Своя девушка. Common feminine noun meaning 'young woman; girlfriend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: She's my girlfriend.
A pretty young woman.

examples.text: У мужчины, мальчик, бывает не только жена. Это моя девушка.
examples.trans: A man, my boy, can have more than just a wife. She's my girlfriend.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('dramatic').

examples.text: Грустная музыка усиливает драматический эффект в суде!
examples.trans: Sad music heightens the dramatic effect in court!

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень драматический выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very dramatic choice.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.
I'm going to Mum's.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('favourite, beloved').
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('favourite, beloved').

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой!
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake!
This is my favourite book.

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой! До вечера, Марина.
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake! See you tonight, Marina.

meanings.note: Art or sound of music. Common feminine noun meaning 'music' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We'll find some music right now.
I like listening to quiet music.

examples.text: Вань, посмотри! — Смотри, работает! Сейчас музыку найдём.
examples.trans: Vanya, look! — Look, it works! We'll find some music right now.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Parenthetical adverb. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'верное').

examples.trans: Well, probably somewhere in the archive.
He has probably already come home.

examples.text: Наверное, что-то серьёзное у вас. Девочка уже две недели лежит в областной клинике!
examples.trans: It must be something serious for you. The girl has been lying in the regional clinic for two weeks already!

meanings.note: + instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'over, above; at' in everyday speech.
смеяться над = to laugh at; form надо before мной

examples.trans: The lamp is above the table.
Don't laugh at me.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start', paired with 'начать'.

examples.trans: When do I start?
The lesson starts at nine.

examples.text: Аркаш, ну что скажешь? Когда начинать?
examples.trans: Arkasha, so what do you say? When do I start?

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Grab him!

Four-eyes! Grab him!

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'insult' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: One more rude insult like that.

examples.text: За все свои оскорбления ты мне ответишь.
examples.trans: You will pay me for all your insults.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'менять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'cancels'.

examples.text: Но это не отменяет того, что ты козел.
examples.trans: But that doesn't change the fact you're a bastard.

examples.text: Но это совсем не отменяет твоей сегодняшней смены.
examples.trans: But that does not cancel your shift today at all.

examples.text: Гость позвонил в ресторан и попросил не отменять бронь.
examples.trans: The guest called the restaurant and asked not to cancel the reservation.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'терпевшая'). Common feminine noun meaning 'female victim' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Потерпевшая, расскажите, что произошло тем вечером.
examples.trans: Victim, tell us what happened that evening.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть потерпевшая.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always female victim.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чувствовать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to feel'.

examples.trans: The guest smelled the pleasant aroma of the dish.

examples.text: Инспектор точно почувствует вкус крепкого алкоголя.
examples.trans: The inspector will definitely taste strong alcohol.

examples.text: Поверь мне, никто не почувствует разницу!
examples.trans: Believe me, nobody will feel the difference!

meanings.note: Single act of betrayal. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to betray'.

examples.trans: I will not betray my native land.
I will not betray my native land!

examples.text: Твой дед в войну родину предал.
examples.trans: Your grandfather betrayed his country in the war.

прежний.gloss: former, previous, the same as before

meanings.note: оставаться прежним = to remain the same as before

examples.trans: The preventive measure remains the same.
He works at his former place.

examples.text: Мера пресечения остаётся прежней. Домашний арест!
examples.trans: The preventive measure remains the same. House arrest!

meanings.note: usually 3rd person: что произошло? = what happened?

examples.trans: What happened?

examples.text: Я не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: I don't know how it happened.

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, простите меня, пожалуйста. Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, please forgive me. I don't know myself how it happened.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'клятый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('cursed').

examples.trans: To that same cursed room.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень проклятый выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very cursed choice.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'тест'). Common masculine noun meaning 'objection, protest' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I object, Your Honor, that is an insult!

examples.text: Костя, мы сейчас быстро отменяем протест.
examples.trans: Kostya, we are overruling the objection right now.

examples.text: Протестую, Ваша честь, выключите эту музыку!
examples.trans: I object, Your Honor, turn off that music!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'тестовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'object, protest'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и протестовать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and object on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют протестовать.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to object.

meanings.note: about something: рассказать о + prepositional
ironic: Сталину расскажите = tell that to Stalin

examples.trans: Tell me what happened.
I'll tell Mum everything.
Tell that to Stalin.

meanings.note: Plural: дети. Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'child' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is my child.
The child is asleep.
Yes! Even a child knows.

meanings.note: Marriage celebration. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вадьба'). Common feminine noun meaning 'wedding' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Watch the movie Wedding on Skype.

examples.text: Макс, зачем ты соврал про нашу будущую свадьбу?
examples.trans: Max, why did you lie about our future wedding?
Then a wedding, and then kids!

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: I'm in the office now.
I'll be right there.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Building for goods storage. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'клад'). Common masculine noun meaning 'warehouse, storage' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это старый заброшенный склад за городом.
examples.trans: It is an old abandoned warehouse outside town.

examples.text: Хорошо, тогда встретимся на этом складе.
examples.trans: Fine, then we will meet at this warehouse.

examples.text: Ищи на складе и быстрее крутись!
examples.trans: Search in the storage and hustle faster!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.trans: You can see it at once.
I understood at once.
Now there's a businesswoman, you can see it at once.

meanings.note: Of things and people. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тарый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('old').
'старый друг' = an old friend. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тарый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('old').

examples.trans: I have an old phone.
This is my old friend.

examples.text: Славик, смотри сюда. Меняю свой новый айфон на твой старый телефон.
examples.trans: Slavik, look here. I'll swap my new iPhone for your old phone.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'court' in everyday Russian.
Common masculine noun meaning 'court' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The court has decided.
He is in court.

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.
Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
That's good like that.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: The one over there. Core Russian det meaning 'that' in everyday speech.
in 'то, что ...' = 'what, the thing that'

examples.trans: That's what you said.
That house is old.
Well, the thing you said.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'силивать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'heighten, intensify'.

examples.text: Грустная музыка усиливает драматический эффект в суде!
examples.trans: Sad music heightens the dramatic effect in court!

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и усиливать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and heighten on time.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.trans: A good day.
What a lovely morning!

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: 3rd-declension feminine noun in -ь. Common feminine noun meaning 'honour; (Ваша честь) Your Honour' in everyday Russian.
Ваша честь = courtroom address to a judge

examples.text: Ваша честь, у нас есть заявление.
examples.trans: Your Honour, we have a statement.
It is a matter of honour.

examples.text: Ваша честь, у нас есть важное заявление.
examples.trans: Your Honour, we have an important statement.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something; somehow', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Did something happen?
Has something happened?
Somehow I'm tired.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'feeling, emotion, sense' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович испытывает к вам чувства.

Sixth sense.

examples.text: Ты же знаешь мои настоящие чувства.
examples.trans: You know my real feelings.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: That's mine.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: эффект снежного кома = snowball effect

examples.trans: That is the snowball effect.
An unexpected effect.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, да вы не волнуйтесь! Это просто эффект снежного кома.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, don't worry! That is simply the snowball effect.
